history.dynasty: Unverified — historians trace the deity's origin to the 17th–18th century
history.summary: Budharaja Temple stands at the foot of Papanga Hill near Papanga village (Bheden block), about 33 km from Bargarh town. Historians place the origin of the deity Budharaja in the 17th or 18th century. The hill is closely linked to the rebellion of freedom fighter Veer Surendra Sai against the British (the Surendra Sai Cave is on the hill). The site also has a Shriram temple, a Yogashram (reached by 250 steps), a mango grove, the Bankhol forest garden and a triangular pond, and is a popular picnic spot. NOTE: do not confuse this temple with the better-documented 18th-century Chauhan Budharaja Temple in Sambalpur city — a different temple sharing the same name.

name: Budharaja Temple
town_description: Papanga is a village in the Bheden block of Bargarh district in western Odisha, set at the foot of the forested Papanga (Budharaja) Hill. Bargarh district, often called the rice bowl of Odisha, was historically a stronghold of the former Patna state and is closely associated with the rebellion of freedom fighter Veer Surendra Sai. The Papanga Hill area combines dense forest, hill-climbing trails and picnic spots with its small shrines.
